advisory: SailCast is advisory. Official forecasts and warnings come first, and the skipper decides.

pickers.edit_sailor: Edit this sailor's skill, boats and times

start.title: Welcome to SailCast
start.admin: Add a spot, a boat and a sailor in Settings to get started. SailCast then rates every hour of the week for them.
start.other: An administrator needs to add a spot, a boat and a sailor before SailCast can rate the week.

forecast.none: SailCast fetches the forecast for a new spot within a minute or two. If this stays, check that Home Assistant can reach the internet.

week.best_day: The best day is {day}, with a score of {score} ({band}).
week.window_rule: A good window needs at least two hours in a row scoring 60 or more, inside your sailing times, and in daylight unless the boat has navigation lights.
week.calendar_sub: Rated for {sailor} ({skill}) in the {boat}. Select a day to see it hour by hour, or a sailing window to add it to a calendar or take it out.
week.not_sailing_day: Not one of your sailing days
week.confidence_title: The three forecast models typically agree within {spread} kt

now.title: Now
now.note: Readings count while they're fresh: two hours for wind and air, three for waves and six for water. Anything not read shows this hour's forecast.
now.note_no_sources: No buoy, airport or sensor reads this spot, so this is the forecast for the hour now under way.
now.note_no_sources_admin: No buoy, airport or sensor reads this spot, so this is the forecast for the hour now under way. Edit the spot in Settings to pick the nearest.
now.wind_height: Measured {height} above the water; shown at {standard}, the height forecasts use.

warnings.title: Official warnings
warnings.meaning: Dinghies and small keelboats are rated not recommended or worse at every skill level while an advisory is in effect. Cruisers get at least caution.
warnings.no_zone_hint: Edit the spot to pick where its official warnings come from.
warnings.no_end: Canada's marine warnings don't say when they end, so SailCast counts each one until the end of the day after it was issued, or until it's lifted.
warnings.meteoalarm_note: Time delays between this website and the www.meteoalarm.org website are possible. For the most up-to-date awareness information as published by the participating National Meteorological and Hydrological Services, please refer to

tip.add: Select to add it to a calendar
tip.take_out: {status}. Select to see it or take it out.

planned.auto_explain: SailCast added {sailor}'s best window for this day and keeps the event in step with the forecast. If you take it out, SailCast won't add another one for this day.
planned.watching: SailCast tells you if the forecast for this time gets worse.
planned.not_watching: You turned off forecast warnings for this sail.
planned.cannot_delete: This calendar ({calendar}) doesn't let Home Assistant delete events, so SailCast only stops watching it. Delete the event in your calendar app.
planned.take_out: Take it out of the calendar
planned.not_yours: Only an administrator, or {sailor} signed in as themselves, can take it out.

add.title: Add to a calendar
add.no_calendars: No calendar here accepts new events. Add a Local Calendar, or connect Google Calendar or CalDAV, in Settings → Devices & services.
add.preview: SailCast forecast for {sailor} in the {boat}. Score {score} ({band}).
add.preview_check: Check the forecast and official warnings again before you go.
add.watch: Tell me if the forecast for this time gets worse
add.hint: SailCast adds the event as you, so the calendar's own permissions apply.
add.not_yours: Only an administrator, or {sailor} signed in as themselves, can add {sailor}'s windows to a calendar.

auto.title: Automatic calendar · {sailor}
auto.switch: Add {sailor}'s best window each day automatically
auto.ahead_hint: Forecasts change most beyond three days.
auto.spots_hint: When windows at different spots overlap, SailCast adds only the best one.
auto.explain: Windows are for the {boat}, {sailor}'s usual boat, inside {sailor}'s sailing times. SailCast adds at most one event a day and keeps it in step with the forecast: it moves the event when the window shifts by 30 minutes or more and takes it out if the window goes away. From 6 PM the evening before, it stops changing the event and warns you instead. Calendars that don't allow changes, such as CalDAV, get warnings only.
auto.off_chip: Add windows to a calendar automatically
auto.off_row: Off. {sailor} adds windows one at a time.

day.confidence: Confidence {confidence}: the three models typically agree within {spread} kt.
day.size_changes: {best} for at least two hours in a row; {worst} at {time} ({why}).
day.wind_label: Wind and gusts through the day
day.tide_current_label: Tide and current through the day

ai.title: AI briefing
ai.note: Written by AI from SailCast's forecast, so it can get things wrong. The ratings and windows come from SailCast's own rules.
ai.changed: The forecast has changed since this was written.
ai.failed: The AI briefing couldn't be written: {message}
ai.bad_answer: The answer didn't look like a briefing. Try again, or pick another AI task in SailCast's options.

map.label: Animated wind map around {spot}
map.point: Point at the map to read the wind
map.tap: Tap the map to read the wind
map.budget: The wind map rests until tomorrow, so SailCast stays within Open-Meteo's free daily calls. The forecast itself keeps going.
map.view_budget: To stay within Open-Meteo's free daily calls, the wind covers only the areas SailCast already has until tomorrow.
map.stale: This is the wind as forecast on {time}; SailCast couldn't fetch a newer one.
map.credits: Wind © Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0), hourly from its best model for the area, with points about 2 km apart up close and wider apart as you zoom out. Map © OpenStreetMap contributors, seamarks © OpenSeaMap. Not for navigation.

sources.title: Where these numbers come from
sources.wind_text: ECMWF IFS, GFS and ICON models through Open-Meteo. SailCast uses the middle value; the spread between the models sets the confidence.
sources.waves_open: The Open-Meteo marine model's nearest cell. Inside an enclosed bay it can read high.
sources.waves_sheltered: From directions this spot is sheltered from, SailCast uses the larger of the local estimate and half the model's height.
sources.current_text: NOAA {station}. NOAA gives slack and peak times; the hours in between are filled in.
sources.nudged: {source} read {difference} {direction} the forecast there at {time}, so the next hours move with it, fading over six hours.
sources.waves_estimate: Worked out from the wind and the open water upwind, measured on the map: © OpenStreetMap contributors, through OpenFreeMap.
sources.waves_estimate_set: Worked out from the wind and {distance} of open water upwind, as set for this spot.
sources.waves_none: None yet: SailCast measures the shoreline when a spot is added.
sources.waves_nudged: {source} read {difference} {direction} the model there at {time}, so the next hours move with it.
sources.on_land: None: the spot's pin is on land. Move it onto the water in Settings.

tide_by.chs: Canadian Hydrographic Service station {station}, in heights above {datum}.
tide_by.rws: Rijkswaterstaat station {station}: the astronomical tide, in heights above {datum}.
tide_by.kartverket: Kartverket, worked out for the pin from {gauge}, in heights above {datum}.
tide_by.worldtides: WorldTides, for the pin, in heights above {datum}.
tide_by.model: Rough: the ocean model's sea level at the pin, in heights above {datum}. Near the coast its times can be an hour or more off, so SailCast shows the curve but no highs and lows from it. Plan with proper tide tables.

warnings_by.nws_pin: National Weather Service alerts for the pin
warnings_by.eccc: Data Source: Environment and Climate Change Canada, {zone}

settings.admin_note: These are the same settings as Settings → Devices & services → SailCast, so a change in either place shows up in both. Only administrators can change them.
settings.read_only_note: Only Home Assistant administrators can change these. You can still pick your own spot, sailor and boat at the top.
settings.sailors_sub: Each sailor rates their own skill. Skill sets the limit for sustained wind; everything else is rated the same at every level.
settings.boats_sub: A boat's size sets where wind, gusts and waves turn to caution, not recommended and dangerous.
settings.spots_sub: Where you sail, and the stations SailCast reads for each spot.
settings.calendar_sub: Copy sailing windows into a calendar to keep the time free, one at a time or automatically.
settings.default_calendar_hint: Any Home Assistant calendar that accepts new events: Local Calendar, Google Calendar or CalDAV. You can pick another one each time.
settings.read_only_calendars: Each sailor also gets a read-only SailCast calendar in Home Assistant: {calendars}. It always shows the current windows, so automations can use it, for example to remind you an hour before a window starts.
settings.nothing_planned: Nothing yet. Select a sailing window in the week or day view to add it to a calendar, or turn on automatic adding. SailCast then keeps an eye on the forecast for those times and tells you if it gets worse.
settings.no_boats_yet: No boats yet. Add one first; every sailor needs a boat.
settings.boat_first: Add a boat first. Every sailor needs at least one.

sailor.skill_hint: Your own judgment of what you can handle. It sets your limit for sustained wind. Gusts, waves, official warnings and dangerous conditions are rated the same at every level.
sailor.when_hint: Tick the days you sail, each with its own hours; sailing windows only fall inside them. Left at sunrise and sunset, a boat with navigation lights can sail at any hour. To change one day, such as a day off, use the hours under that day in the week.
sailor.ideal_hint: Narrows the ideal wind for each boat. Leave empty to use the boat's range.
sailor.coldest_hint: Scores drop in colder air. Leave empty for {default}.
sailor.comfort_hint: Comfort changes scores, never a safety rating.
sailor.user_hint: SailCast opens on this sailor for them.

hours.title: Sailing hours: {day}
hours.off_hint: No sailing windows on this day.
hours.set_hint: Choose a start and an end.
hours.hint: This changes this day only. The usual hours stay as they are.

boat.size_hint: {lengths}. Caution from {caution} kt, dangerous from {dangerous} kt.
boat.lights_hint: Turn on if the boat has working navigation lights. Hours after dark then count too, within the sailor's times.
boat.limits: Limits for this size, the same at every skill level

spot.map_label: Map of the spot. Select the water to move the pin.
spot.pin_hint: {position}. Select the water to move the pin, or drag it; arrow keys move it too. The circle is the area the wind map will show. ▲ tide, ◆ current, ● buoy and ■ airport nearby.
spot.radius_km: Wind map area: {value} km around the pin
spot.radius_miles: Wind map area: {value} mi around the pin
spot.offshore_hint: Wind from these directions blows away from the shore.
spot.exposed_hint: Directions with open water, where waves can build.
spot.sources_hint: SailCast suggests the nearest of each as you move the pin. Tides come from NOAA, the Canadian Hydrographic Service, Rijkswaterstaat or Kartverket, and anywhere from WorldTides with a key in SailCast's options. Warnings come from the National Weather Service, Environment and Climate Change Canada and MeteoAlarm. Buoys come from NDBC, and airport reports from anywhere.
spot.sources_failed: Couldn't look up nearby sources. You can save without them and add them later.
spot.sensors_hint: Readings from your own weather station or a boat's instruments come first, ahead of the buoy and airport. SailCast takes them to be at the spot.
spot.fetch_hint: Optional. SailCast measures the open water each way from the map; set one distance here only to override it.
spot.shore_measuring: Measuring the open water around the pin…
spot.on_land: This pin is on land. Drop it on the water where you sail, so SailCast can work out waves and fetch.
spot.shore_open: Open water reaches {distance} toward the {direction}, and the spot is open to the sea from {open}.
spot.notes_hint: Local knowledge for the AI, used in the briefing and when you ask Assist about sailing, such as when the sea breeze fills in or where it gets rough. It never changes a rating.

error.name_taken: Another one already has this name.
error.radius_out_of_range: Make the area 2 to 50 km (about 1 to 30 miles).
error.length_out_of_range: Enter a length between 1 and 50 m (3 and 164 ft).
error.end_before_start: The end has to be after the start.
error.ideal_high_below_low: The top of the range has to be above the bottom.
error.calendar_read_only: That calendar can't take new events.
error.unknown_user: That Home Assistant user no longer exists.
error.boat_in_use: {sailor} sails only this boat. Give them another boat first.
error.fetch_out_of_range: Make the open water between 0.05 and 100 km (about 0.03 to 60 miles).
error.invalid_sensor: Pick a sensor for each reading, or none.

advice.warning_not_recommended: {event} in effect. Not a day for a {size}, whatever your skill.
advice.warning_caution: {event} in effect. Reef early and stay close to the harbor.
advice.light_air: Very light air. Expect long stretches of drifting.
advice.gusty: Gusty. Be ready to ease the sheets in the puffs.
advice.gusty_dinghy: Gusty. Be ready to ease the sheets in the puffs and hike hard.
advice.over_limit_hour: Wind above your {limit} kt limit around {time}.
advice.over_limit: Wind above your {limit} kt limit between {start} and {end}.
advice.near_limit: Close to your {limit} kt limit at times.
advice.reef: Consider a reef before you leave the mooring.
advice.depower: Plan to depower: flatten the sails and reef if you can.
advice.against_flood: Wind against the flood around {span}: expect steeper chop.
advice.against_ebb: Wind against the ebb around {span}: expect steeper chop.
advice.offshore: The wind blows off the beach. If you capsize you will drift away from shore, so stay close in.
advice.rain_visibility: Rain likely ({chance}%), with visibility down to {visibility} nm.

reason.wind_over_limit: wind {wind} kt, over your {limit} kt limit

skill_text.advanced: No wind limit. Conditions guidance only

datum.NAP: NAP, close to mean sea level
